languageDiagnosisCard.description: Controls how the AI asks, judges and grades in the diagnosis chat. Applies to every workspace. German only for now.
languageDiagnosisCard.hint: Controls the flow, the question style and the output format of the test. Four placeholders in the text are filled in: '{language}' with the language of the test, '{grading}' with the grading rules below, '{levels}' with the descriptions from the Levels A1 to C2 card and '{examples}' with the example sentences from there. A placeholder you delete is appended at the end, so the AI never loses it.

diagnosisPlanCard.title: Language Test questions
diagnosisPlanCard.description: Decides which questions the Language Test asks. Each row is one question with one of two task types. Choice means clicking and needs answer options with at least one marked correct. Free text means typing and needs only the question text. The solution on a free text is optional and decides who marks it: with a solution the code checks the answer word for word, without one the AI judges it at the end. Anything that belongs before the question, a short reading text or an everyday situation, simply goes into the question text. The order is the order in the test and runs from easy to hard. Either you write everything yourself, or you let the AI write it once and read it through. The test itself then runs without a single AI call. The AI assigns the level A1 to C2 at the end from the answers, not per question.
diagnosisPlanCard.languageHint: The test is in German, so questions and options are too.
diagnosisPlanCard.freeTextHint: At least 2 free-text questions without a solution are required. Only those does the AI judge itself, and only they give the level a real writing sample.
diagnosisPlanCard.optionsHint: Mark exactly one correct. Several are allowed if the question says so.
diagnosisPlanCard.answersHint: Leave it empty if the AI should judge the answer. If you enter a solution, the code checks the typed answer and this question needs no AI at all. One solution per line, every line counts as correct. Capitalisation and a final punctuation mark are ignored, accents and umlauts are not. Short solutions give the learner a one-line box, whole sentences the big one.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByCodeHint: Checked without AI. The typed answer has to match one of the solutions.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByAiHint: The AI judges this answer at the end, using the grading rules and the level examples from the AI behaviour tab. This row counts towards the required writing samples.
diagnosisPlanCard.generate: Let the AI write the questions
diagnosisPlanCard.generatingHint: This takes about a minute. The AI writes a complete set of questions, and you can change every one of them afterwards.

Delete a placeholder and that piece is simply missing.

toolContextBudgetCard.title: Tools context budget
toolContextBudgetCard.hint: How much text from the material (in characters) the tools hand to the model. Mind map, podcast, schedule and data table use the whole value: the mind map splits it across the chosen material, the podcast fills up one by one, schedule and data table cut their material into packets of this size and make one call per packet. Flashcards, vocab cards, quiz, vocabulary and grammar exercises take only what the requested number of exercises needs, about 6,700 characters per exercise, whatever does not fit comes up in the next set. This value is their ceiling. If the configured model cannot take that much, it refuses the job with an error, then this value has to come down.

summary_read_max_facts.title: Fact cap per file

summary_call_timeout_seconds.title: AI call timeout

auth.heading: 2. Authentication and user account
auth.intro: Access to the platform is provided through an account on this platform. The following data is stored in our database:
auth.itemPassword: Password, stored only as a bcrypt hash, never in plain text
auth.item4: Language level (if determined via the AI chat test, deletable at any time)

auth.outro:
Sign-in currently runs against an account on this platform. The password is stored as a hash only and cannot be derived from it. A connection to the central sign-in of TH Lübeck is planned, after which this platform will hold no password.
Legal basis: Art. 6 (1) (e) GDPR (performance of a task carried out in the public interest).
Retention period: until the user account is deleted.

cookies.heading: 3. Cookies and local storage
cookies.intro: This platform uses only technically necessary cookies and storage mechanisms:
cookies.sessionBody: An HttpOnly cookie used for authentication (valid for 24 hours). Without this cookie, login is not possible.
cookies.storageBody: Temporary storage of filter settings in the browser (automatically cleared when the tab is closed).
cookies.outro: No tracking, analytics or marketing cookies are used. Cookie data is not shared with third parties.

jobs.heading: 4. Processing of user uploads and job data
jobs.intro: When you use the platform, uploaded files (e.g. videos, PDFs, presentations, audio files) and the results derived from them (e.g. transcripts, summaries) are stored in your workspace. For each processing job, the following metadata is also stored:
jobs.retention: Uploaded files and the results derived from them remain stored in your workspace until you or a workspace administrator deletes them. Job metadata for individual processing jobs is retained only to a limited extent. The most recent jobs are kept and older ones are removed automatically. At the latest when the pilot project ends, all workspaces and the files in them are deleted. If you want that earlier, an email to the address above or a message through the feedback form is enough.

adminAccess.heading: 5. Access by administrators
adminAccess.intro: People with the relevant permission — in particular administrators, as well as anyone assigned the "User statistics" right — can view the following data for individual user accounts:
adminAccess.item1: Chat messages sent, verbatim, with workspace and time
adminAccess.item2: Services used, with status and file name
adminAccess.item4: Presence times on the platform (to the day)
adminAccess.item6: For support: temporarily signing in as the affected person ("takeover"), start and end are logged
adminAccess.outro:
This access serves the technical administration of the platform, troubleshooting, and quality assurance. It is limited to the people who have been granted this permission as part of their duties.
Legal basis: Art. 6 (1) (e) GDPR (performance of a task carried out in the public interest).
Retention period: matches the retention of the underlying data (chat history and workspace membership persist until the workspace or user account is deleted; job metadata as described in section 4; the takeover log is kept indefinitely).

thirdParty.heading: 6. Third parties and external services
thirdParty.intro: Which AI providers are used is configured through the platform's administration. The following external services are currently in use:
thirdParty.kisskiBody: Language models and transcription services. Texts and audio content are processed in this context. KISSKI is a service of Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) and is subject to German data protection law. Processing takes place under a data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR.
thirdParty.mylabBody: Language models operated by Hochschule Lübeck itself. Processing takes place on the university's own servers; no data is transmitted to external providers.
thirdParty.deeplBody: Translation service for automatic translations. Processing takes place at DeepL SE and is subject to European data protection law.
thirdParty.hetznerBody: Cloud storage for uploaded files. Storage takes place at Hetzner Online GmbH on servers in Germany.
thirdParty.youtubeBody: Embedded videos in workspaces. The player loads only after a click on the video, no data flows before that. When loading and playing, Google LLC (USA) receives the IP address and device data. The embed uses YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com). The transcript of a video is entered by the teacher and stored on the platform, it is not fetched from YouTube.
thirdParty.outro: For the external services, only the content required for the respective function is transmitted, and no further storage takes place there. Uploaded files remain in object storage until they are deleted.

logs.heading: 7. Server log files
logs.intro: When this website is accessed, the web server automatically records information in so-called server log files. This includes:

whatIsKis.q: What is KIS and what is it for?
whatIsKis.a: KIS is a pilot project at TH Lübeck. It brings together two things: the AI assistant Francis, who answers from the materials stored in a workspace, and the services you use to produce teaching material.

vsChatgpt.q: How is the AI assistant Francis different from ChatGPT?
vsChatgpt.a:
The AI assistant Francis is built on RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): it looks up the matching passages in your workspace's materials and answers only from those, attaching a source to every sentence, which opens the exact spot in the document. Anything beyond that he turns down. The closer comparison is Gemini Notebook by Google (formerly NotebookLM), not ChatGPT.

On top of that, processing runs with providers in Germany, not in the US. Our data is not used for training.

KIS itself is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

moduleServiceTool.q: What is the difference between a workspace, a service and a tool?
moduleServiceTool.a: A workspace is a course room with materials and chat. A service stands on its own, such as translation or screencast. A tool sits in the studio inside a workspace, such as flashcards or quizzes.

costs.q: Does this cost anything, is there a limit?
costs.a:
Using it costs you nothing.

Part of the models run through KISSKI at GWDG, under a strict quota shared across the whole university: 2 requests per second, 15 per minute, 900 per hour, 21,000 per day and 350,000 per month. If other people have that quota busy right now, a request can come back with an error.

THL myLab, the second provider, has no fixed limit at the moment. On the second Thursday of each month from 8 pm, its systems get updated, and it can be unreachable during that window.

gdpr.q: Is my data safe and GDPR-compliant?
gdpr.a:
Yes. Processing happens at THL myLab, GWDG/KISSKI and DeepL, all in Germany or the EU. None of them train on the data.

What is stored in detail, and for how long, is set out in the privacy policy.

hosting.q: Who runs the platform, where are the servers?
hosting.a: The platform runs at Hetzner in Germany, uploaded files are held in Hetzner Object Storage.

models.q: Which AI models are used and who decides that?
models.a:
The KIS team configures the models centrally. They run at three providers: THL myLab at TH Lübeck, KISSKI from GWDG in Göttingen, and DeepL for translating files.

In the chat with the AI assistant Francis, gemma4-31b answers. Which model sits behind the other services changes from time to time. When a service has more than one provider set up, for example translation, text to audio or the image generator, you pick it yourself in the form.

whoSees.q: Who can see my materials and my chat?
whoSees.a: Materials and chat belong to the workspace and are visible to its members. A small circle of people with the corresponding permission may inspect them for technical support, as set out in the privacy policy.

afterPilot.q: What happens to my data once the pilot project ends?
afterPilot.a: At the latest when the pilot project ends, your workspaces and uploaded files are deleted. If you want that sooner, send us an email or a message through the feedback form.

notFound.q: Why does the AI assistant Francis not know something that is in the document?
notFound.a:
The AI assistant Francis does not search a whole document at once, he searches it in sections. If the answer is spread across many places, or sits only in a table or a graphic, he may not find it.

What helps: narrow the question, name the chapter, or leave only that one document active in the source selection.

generalQuestions.q: Why does he not answer general questions?
generalQuestions.a: That is deliberate. The AI assistant Francis is tied to the materials of the workspace so that nothing enters an answer that is not in them. He is not meant for anything else.

trust.q: Can I trust the answers, and what are the sources on each sentence for?
trust.a: The small sources behind a sentence lead to the spot in the document it came from. One click opens and highlights it. Use them to check anything that matters, AI answers can be wrong.

studentView.q: What do students see when I give them access to a workspace?
studentView.a: Materials, chat and the tools in the studio. Not visible are the workspace settings, the participant management and the figures for the whole workspace. You can check this yourself in the student view.

bugReport.q: Where do I report a problem?
bugReport.a: Through the feedback form. Say what you did and what happened, that saves a follow-up question.

presentationTemplate.q: What does my own template need for the presentation service?
presentationTemplate.a: A pptx or potx file up to 30 MB without macros. The first slide master counts. Layouts need a heading, otherwise they are skipped. Image fields are needed for images to be created. The image style is described in English.
